chunks: Al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deviation of our companions towards the left regarding the Qiblah, and the reason for it.

He said: 'Indeed, the Black Stone, when it was sent down from Paradise and placed in its position, the pillars of the Sanctuary were made from where the light reaches it, the light of the Stone. So they are four miles to the right of the Ka'bah and eight miles to its left, all twelve miles. So if a person deviates to the right, he goes out of the boundary of the Qiblah due to the scarcity of the pillars of the Sanctuary, and if he deviates to the left, he is not considered to have gone out of the boundary of the Qiblah.'

key_terms.أَنْصَاب: Pillars or markers (here referring to the extent/boundary)

ai.seo_question: Why is it permissible to face slightly left during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the permissibility of deviating to the left during prayer. The Imam explains that the Black Stone, originally from Paradise, emits a spiritual light that defines the sacred boundaries of the Kaaba; this light extends eight miles to the left but only four miles to the right. Consequently, while turning right may take one outside the valid Qiblah range, turning left remains within the sanctified radius, offering a theological basis for the flexibility in prayer orientation.
